course_position.stage_name: Toward B1 - Complex Conversations and Narratives

lesson_intent.one_sentence_goal: Practice telling a short sequence with först, sedan, and till slut.
lesson_intent.real_life_context: A colleague tells a simple story about a morning, commute, or weekend errand.
lesson_intent.communicative_function: Narrating events in a clear order.

dialogue_task.scenario: Anna and Erik talk about a morning that did not go exactly as planned.

main_focus.name: sequencing past events
main_focus.description: Use time adverbs to organize a short story in preterite.
model_examples: Sedan tog jag cykeln, och till slut kom jag fram.
main_focus.desired_presence: Use sequence words naturally 3-4 times across the dialogue.

allowed_supporting_grammar: reported speech with one simple att clause
simple reason clauses with för att

useful_chunks: Hoppas resten av dagen blir lugnare.
vocabulary_target.desired_presence: Use sequence chunks to make the event order easy to follow.

dialogue_shape.opening: One speaker asks why the other seems tired or arrived late.
dialogue_shape.middle: A short sequence of events is told with clear order markers.
dialogue_shape.ending: The listener reacts and the conversation turns toward the rest of the day.

target_complexity.repetition: sequence markers should be prominent but natural

focus: what happens first, next, and finally

sentence_focus: one sentence about missing a bus or being delayed
one sentence summarizing a short event sequence
